quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Questions about the relocation can be sent to the facilities mailbox, which will be monitored daily until the end of the month.
Beyond the equipment, anyone who requires special arrangements, such as accessible parking or a height-adjustable desk, should inform the office manager by the end of next week.
Company equipment, including monitors and docking stations, will be transferred by the facilities team and does not need to be packed by employees.
Once the move is complete, an orientation session will be held to explain the new layout, the meeting-room booking system, and the emergency exits.
Following the lease decision announced last month, the finance department will relocate to the third floor of the Harbor Building on the first of October.
To minimize disruption, the move has been scheduled for a weekend, and staff are asked to pack personal items into the crates that will be delivered on Thursday.
quests.hint: In a workplace memo, each paragraph part has a job: announce, give instructions, offer support, and invite questions. Which sentence announces the change, and which sentence points to a contrast with what employees must do themselves?
quests.explanation: The announcement comes first, the second sentence gives employees their task, the third sentence contrasts it with what the facilities team will do, "beyond the equipment" adds a further request, "once the move is complete" looks ahead, and the last sentence invites questions. The memo moves from decision to action to support.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Economists studying the episode argue that companies keeping small reserves of critical parts recovered noticeably faster than those relying on just-in-time delivery.
Container ships waiting offshore delayed the arrival of components that factories needed for their assembly lines.
As a result, many firms are now reconsidering the balance between cost efficiency and resilience.
Several manufacturers, unable to obtain a single missing part, were forced to reduce production even though their other materials were plentiful.
When a major port closed for repairs last year, the effects spread far beyond the shipping industry.
The resulting shortage of finished goods pushed prices upward, and retailers that depended on those products lost sales during the busiest season.
quests.hint: "The resulting shortage" and "the episode" each summarize earlier material. Which sentences do they refer to?
quests.explanation: The closure is the trigger, delayed ships are the first effect, the factories' reduced output is the second, the shortage and higher prices are the third, the economists' analysis interprets the whole event, and "as a result" states the business response. Each nominal phrase compresses what came before.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Sunscreens are often chosen by their protection factor, yet that number describes only one type of ultraviolet radiation.
Because UVA exposure contributes to skin aging and to some cancers, dermatologists recommend products labeled broad-spectrum.
Clothing, shade, and sunglasses should complement lotion rather than replace it, since no single measure provides complete protection.
The factor measures protection against UVB rays, which cause sunburn, but says little about UVA rays, which penetrate deeper into the skin.
Even the best product loses its effect if too little is applied, and studies suggest that most people use less than half the amount tested in laboratories.
Reapplying every two hours, and after swimming, is therefore as important as the initial choice of product.
quests.hint: "Yet" and "even" both signal that the reader should expect a limit or surprise. Which sentences contain each limit?
quests.explanation: The first sentence states a common practice and limits it, the second explains the limit, the third gives a recommendation, the fourth adds a second limit about quantity, the fifth draws a practical conclusion with "therefore", and the last sentence widens the advice. "Initial choice" refers to the product recommended earlier.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: The customer service team recorded a sharp rise in complaints during the second week of the software update.
Because the update had been tested only on recent devices, the problem had gone unnoticed until customers began to report it.
The team will review the results of this change in six months and report its conclusions to senior management.
To prevent a recurrence, the company has added a range of older devices to its standard testing procedure.
An initial analysis showed that most of the complaints came from users of older tablets, whose screens displayed the new interface incorrectly.
The engineers released a corrective patch within five days, and the number of complaints returned to its normal level shortly afterwards.
quests.hint: A report moves from symptom to cause, to remedy, and to prevention. Which sentence gives the cause, and which describes how it will be avoided in the future?
quests.explanation: The complaints are the symptom, the analysis identifies the group affected, "because" explains why the problem was missed, the patch is the remedy, "to prevent a recurrence" gives the long-term action, and the last sentence describes the review. "This change" refers to the new testing procedure.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: These should include torches with spare batteries, bottled water, non-perishable food, and a battery-powered radio for updates.
Power cuts are usually brief, but a prolonged outage can quickly turn a minor inconvenience into a serious problem.
Finally, a written list of emergency contacts is worth keeping, since mobile phone batteries may not last through a long outage.
Households that prepare in advance cope far better, and the most important step is to gather essential supplies in a single, accessible place.
Beyond food safety, those who rely on medical devices ought to register with their electricity provider, which can then prioritize them during restoration.
Because fridges and freezers stop working, families should also know how long food remains safe and keep the doors closed as much as possible.
quests.hint: "These" and "beyond food safety" both build on something said in an earlier sentence. What?
quests.explanation: The problem is introduced, preparation is the general solution, "these" lists the supplies, the food-safety advice comes from the fact that fridges stop working, "beyond food safety" moves on to medical needs, and "finally" closes the list. The advice moves from the general to the specific.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: A satellite does not stay in orbit because gravity is absent; on the contrary, gravity is what keeps it there.
The result is a continual fall around the planet rather than into it.
The satellite is constantly falling toward the Earth, but it also moves sideways at enormous speed.
Because of that sideways motion, the ground curves away beneath it as fast as it falls.
This is why the International Space Station circles the planet about every ninety minutes, whereas satellites in much higher orbits take a full day.
Lower orbits require greater speeds, since gravity is stronger closer to the Earth.
quests.hint: "On the contrary" corrects a belief. Which sentence states the belief, and which sentence uses "this" to point to a general rule?
quests.explanation: A common misunderstanding is corrected, the two motions are described, "because of that sideways motion" explains the curve, the result is summarized, the rule about speed and height follows, and "this is why" applies it to a real example. "Whereas" contrasts low and high orbits.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: However, the estimated construction cost exceeds the budget available for this phase of the project by nearly thirty percent.
We would welcome a revised version that reduces the scale of the building, and we can arrange a meeting to discuss possible adjustments.
For that reason, the committee regrets that it cannot proceed with the proposal in its current form.
Thank you for submitting your proposal for the new visitor center, which the committee reviewed carefully at its meeting on Tuesday.
We were impressed by the originality of the design and by the clear way in which you explained the intended use of each space.
Please let us know by the end of the month whether you would like to take up this invitation.
quests.hint: A polite refusal usually gives thanks and praise before the difficulty. Which sentences do that, and which sentence introduces the difficulty?
quests.explanation: The thanks come first, the praise softens the news, "however" introduces the problem, "for that reason" states the decision, the invitation offers a way forward, and the last sentence refers to it as "this invitation". The letter follows a diplomatic order.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Families moved in large numbers from the countryside, and towns such as Manchester grew from modest markets into industrial centers within a few decades.
The modern city, with its regulations and public services, is in many ways a product of that difficult period.
Before the eighteenth century, most people in Britain lived in villages and earned their living from agriculture.
The spread of mechanized factories, first in textiles and later in iron and coal, created a demand for workers in a small number of locations.
Public alarm about these conditions eventually led to reforms, including laws on sanitation, factory hours, and the construction of proper drains.
Housing was built quickly and cheaply, and overcrowded districts without clean water or sewers became breeding grounds for disease.
quests.hint: "These conditions" and "that difficult period" both name something described earlier. Which sentences do they refer to?
quests.explanation: The old rural life is the starting point, factories create demand, workers move, the towns grow, the housing is poor, "these conditions" leads to reform, and the last sentence links the past to today. Time phrases and nominal references both mark the progress.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: A child video-calling a grandparent or building a game with a friend is engaged very differently from one watching an endless stream of clips.
Adults who follow the same rules themselves tend to find that their children accept them more readily.
Parents often worry that their children spend too many hours in front of screens, but the length of time is only part of the picture.
Nevertheless, excessive use can displace sleep, exercise, and face-to-face play, all of which are essential for healthy development.
Researchers increasingly emphasize what children are doing, and with whom, rather than counting minutes alone.
Families are therefore advised to set clear limits at bedtime and during meals, and to keep devices out of bedrooms overnight.
quests.hint: "Nevertheless" limits a point that has just been made. Which sentence makes that point?
quests.explanation: A worry is stated and qualified, the researchers' shift in emphasis follows, the examples illustrate different kinds of use, "nevertheless" reminds the reader of the risks, "therefore" leads to advice, and the last sentence adds a note about example-setting. "The same rules" refers to the limits just described.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: To make this system work, the salary must be set below the average monthly income, not at the level of the best months.
A common remedy is to pay every client payment into a separate account and to draw a fixed monthly salary from it.
Freelancers often struggle to budget because their income varies from month to month, while most of their bills stay the same.
Once the salary has been fixed, a proportion should also be set aside for taxes as soon as each payment arrives, which avoids an unpleasant surprise at the end of the year.
After a few months, the account itself shows whether the chosen salary is realistic and can be adjusted accordingly.
In good months, the surplus remains in the account, and in lean months, it covers the gap.
quests.hint: A reference to a system and a clause about a fixed salary both depend on earlier steps. Which steps?
quests.explanation: The problem comes first, the remedy is described, the surplus and lean months explain how it works, "to make this system work" states a condition, the tax advice follows the fixing of the salary, and the final sentence describes later adjustment. "Accordingly" links the adjustment to what the account shows.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Cooks who understand these processes can therefore control texture and flavor deliberately instead of relying on chance.
This reaction explains why toasted bread and roasted meat taste so different from their raw or boiled forms.
Vegetables, by contrast, are softened by heat, which breaks down the fibers that give them their crunch and makes them easier to chew and digest.
Heat causes the proteins in an egg to unfold and bond with one another, which turns the transparent liquid into a firm solid.
Cooking does more than make food warmer; it changes the structure of the ingredients themselves.
Browning, which occurs when sugars and proteins react at high temperatures, creates hundreds of new flavor compounds.
quests.hint: "By contrast" sets one example against another. Which sentence gives the example that it is contrasted with?
quests.explanation: The general claim comes first, the egg example shows heat making something firm, the vegetable example shows the opposite, browning adds a third process, "this reaction" refers to browning, and "these processes" summarizes all of them in the conclusion.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: A rehearsal with the finished slides in front of a colleague often exposes unclear passages and timing problems that are invisible to the speaker alone.
Following up with a concise summary within a day reinforces the message and shows respect for the client's time.
Slides work best when they illustrate the argument rather than repeat it, so text should be kept to a minimum.
During the meeting itself, pausing to invite questions keeps the audience engaged and reveals any doubts that need to be addressed.
A successful client presentation begins long before the meeting, with a clear understanding of what the audience needs to decide.
The presenter should identify the single most important message and then select only the evidence that supports it.
quests.hint: The advice follows the timeline of a presentation. Which sentences deal with preparation, which with the meeting, and which with afterwards?
quests.explanation: The overall claim comes first, message and evidence are chosen, the slides are designed, the finished slides are rehearsed, questions are invited during the meeting, and the follow-up comes afterwards. "The finished slides" and "the meeting itself" both point to earlier stages.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: In most parliamentary systems, a proposed law begins as a draft known as a bill.
Committees examine the amended text, hear evidence from experts, and report their findings back to the full chamber.
The bill is introduced by a minister or a member of the legislature and receives a formal first reading, at which its title is announced.
Only after both houses have agreed, and the head of state has signed it, does the bill become law.
It is then debated in detail, and amendments may be proposed by members who wish to change particular provisions.
If the chamber approves the final version, the bill passes to the second house, which follows a similar procedure.
quests.hint: "The amended text" and "the final version" refer to stages of the same document. Which sentences create each stage?
quests.explanation: The draft is introduced, read, debated and amended, examined by committees, approved by the chamber, passed to the second house, and finally signed. "Only after both houses have agreed" places the last step after everything else.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Buying a used car can save a great deal of money, but it also carries risks that a careful buyer should anticipate.
A test drive on both slow streets and fast roads can reveal noises, vibrations, and handling problems that are not obvious in a parked car.
If the car passes those checks, an independent mechanic can inspect it for hidden faults, for which most garages charge a modest fee.
The first step is to establish a realistic budget that includes insurance, tax, and likely maintenance as well as the purchase price.
Armed with the mechanic's report, the buyer can negotiate the price or walk away with confidence.
With a shortlist in hand, the buyer should ask each seller for the vehicle's service history and compare it with the mileage shown.
quests.hint: "Those checks" refers to actions already described. Which sentences describe them?
quests.explanation: The general claim comes first, the budget is the first step, the shortlist leads to the service-history check, the test drive is a further check, "if the car passes those checks" leads to the mechanic's inspection, and the report supports the final decision. Each step depends on the one before.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: This intermediate behavior makes it possible to control the flow of current with great precision.
In insulators such as rubber or glass, by contrast, the electrons are held tightly in place and cannot move freely.
These free electrons can drift through the material when a voltage is applied, forming an electric current.
Metals conduct electricity well because some of their electrons are not bound to individual atoms.
Semiconductors, including silicon, lie between these extremes, since a small amount of energy or a trace of impurity can release their electrons.
It is the basis of the transistors that operate every modern computer and phone.
quests.hint: "These extremes" refers to two opposite cases. Which sentences describe them?
quests.explanation: The conducting case is stated, its mechanism is explained, the insulating case is contrasted, the semiconductors are placed between the two, "this intermediate behavior" states the significance, and "it" links that control to modern technology. "These free electrons" and "these extremes" both refer back.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: The change was recommended by the finance team, who found that paper claims took an average of three weeks to process and were frequently lost.
Employees who are unfamiliar with these procedures can attend one of the training sessions listed on the intranet.
From the start of the next quarter, employees will submit expense claims through an online portal instead of on paper forms.
Claims that match the company's guidelines are approved within two working days, whereas exceptional items are forwarded to a manager for review.
The finance team will evaluate the system after six months and adjust it in response to staff feedback.

quests.hint: "The change" and "these procedures" each point back to something described earlier. What?
quests.explanation: The new policy is announced, its justification follows, the rules of the new system are explained, the approval routes are compared with "whereas", the training refers to "these procedures", and the last sentence describes the future evaluation. The policy moves from decision to reason to practice.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: In the Amazon, this process contributes a substantial share of the moisture that later falls as rain.
Trees draw water from the soil through their roots and release it into the atmosphere from their leaves, a process known as transpiration.
When large areas are cleared, less water enters the air, and rainfall in the surrounding region can decline.
Large forests influence not only the air quality of a region but also the amount of rain that falls there.
Protecting forests is therefore relevant to farmers and city dwellers who live far from the trees themselves.
Reduced rainfall, in turn, makes the remaining forest drier and more vulnerable to fire.
quests.hint: "This process" and "reduced rainfall" each name something introduced earlier. Which sentences supply them?
quests.explanation: The claim comes first, transpiration is defined, the Amazon example uses "this process", clearing reduces the moisture, "reduced rainfall" names the consequence, and "therefore" leads to a wider conclusion. "In turn" shows that the last effect is caused by the previous one.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Adjusting sleep patterns a few days before departure eases the transition to the new time zone.
Once on board, passengers are advised to drink water regularly, since cabin air is very dry and dehydration increases fatigue.
Wearing loose clothing and comfortable shoes makes this easier, and a light sweater deals with the temperature changes.
Long flights can be tiring, but sensible preparation reduces the discomfort considerably.
Moving around the cabin every hour or two, or at least stretching the legs in the seat, helps to keep the blood circulating.
On arrival, exposure to daylight helps the body clock to adapt more quickly.
quests.hint: The advice follows a timeline, from before the flight to after it. Which sentence belongs to each stage?
quests.explanation: The general claim comes first, preparation before departure comes next, advice on board follows, movement is a specific recommendation, clothing makes movement easier, and arrival is the final stage. "This" in the fifth sentence refers to moving around.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: The researchers caution, however, that the participants were volunteers and may have been more motivated than the average employee.
After eight weeks, the group that took regular walks scored significantly higher on the test and reported less tiredness in the afternoons.
Concentration was measured weekly with a standard attention test, and participants also reported their fatigue levels.
Two hundred employees were randomly assigned either to take a five-minute walk every ninety minutes or to continue working without scheduled breaks.
They recommend larger trials in a wider range of workplaces before firm conclusions can be drawn.
This study examined whether short daily breaks improve concentration among office workers who spend most of the day at computers.
quests.hint: A research summary usually states the question, the method, the results, and the limits. Which sentence gives the limits, and how do you know?
quests.explanation: The question comes first, the design describes who did what, the measurements explain how effects were judged, the results follow the eight weeks, "however" introduces a limitation, and the last sentence gives a recommendation. "They" in the final sentence refers to the researchers.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: That atmosphere attracted customers who, for a small entrance fee, could read newspapers, exchange news, and discuss politics and business.
Coffee reached Europe in the seventeenth century, and by the 1650s the first coffeehouses had opened in Oxford and London.
One such institution, which began as a coffeehouse for shipping merchants, grew into the insurance market that still bears its founder's name.
Unlike taverns, which served alcohol, these establishments offered a stimulating drink that encouraged conversation rather than drowsiness.
Merchants soon began to use particular coffeehouses as meeting places for deals, and some of these gatherings developed into permanent institutions.
The coffeehouse thus became a setting in which information circulated freely and new commercial ideas took shape.
quests.hint: "That atmosphere" and "one such institution" both refer back. What do they refer to?
quests.explanation: The arrival of coffee is dated, the drink distinguishes the new places from taverns, "that atmosphere" leads to the customers' activities, merchants turn the places into meeting points, "one such institution" gives an example, and "thus" states a conclusion. Each reference needs its earlier source.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Because rooms near windows are often heated, the air there can become very dry, so grouping plants together or placing a tray of damp pebbles nearby raises the humidity.
Houseplants that thrived in summer often decline in winter, not because they are neglected but because their conditions have changed.
Light matters more than water in this season, so plants should stand close to a window, although their leaves should not touch the cold glass.
Overwatering at this time of year is the most common mistake, since the excess moisture cannot be used and encourages root rot.
Shorter days mean less light, and growth slows as a result, so the plants need much less water than before.
With these adjustments, most plants survive until spring, when longer days signal that it is time to resume normal care.
quests.hint: "Than water" and "near windows" both link a sentence to an earlier one. Which sentences do they connect?
quests.explanation: The problem and its cause come first, less light means less water is needed, overwatering is the mistake that follows, the window advice builds on the comparison between light and water, the humidity advice builds on the window, and the last sentence sums up the result. "These adjustments" refers to the advice given in the previous sentences.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Funding for the workshops was approved in principle but postponed until the next financial year, when more money would be available.
Members first reviewed three proposals: new equipment for the laboratory, a series of staff workshops, and repairs to the ventilation system.
The remaining proposal, for laboratory equipment, was returned to its authors with a request for a more detailed cost comparison.
The committee met on Wednesday to decide how to spend the remaining budget for the year.
The chair thanked the members and confirmed that the next meeting would be held in three weeks' time.
The ventilation repairs were judged to be the most urgent, since inspectors had already issued a warning about air quality.
quests.hint: "The remaining proposal" only makes sense if other proposals have already been dealt with. Which sentences deal with them?
quests.explanation: The meeting's purpose comes first, the proposals are listed, the most urgent is decided, the second is approved with a delay, "the remaining proposal" is the third and last, and the chair closes the meeting. "Remaining" indicates the last item.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: The proportion required depends on how contagious a disease is, and highly infectious diseases such as measles need very high coverage.
When a large proportion of a population is immune, an infection struggles to find new hosts and eventually dies out locally.
Vaccines protect the people who receive them, but they also reduce the spread of disease within a community.
This indirect protection, known as herd immunity, shields those who cannot be vaccinated, such as newborn babies and people with weakened defenses.
Maintaining high coverage is therefore a shared responsibility as well as a personal choice.
If vaccination rates fall below that level, outbreaks become possible again, even in places where the disease had been rare for years.
quests.hint: "That level" refers to a number that has been described. Which sentence describes it?
quests.explanation: The general claim comes first, the community effect is explained, "this indirect protection" is named, the required proportion depends on the disease, "that level" refers to that proportion, and "therefore" states the conclusion. "Again" implies that outbreaks had happened before.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Taking a moment to write a precise line thus saves time for both the sender and the reader.
A recipient often decides whether to open a message on the basis of the subject line alone.
Vague phrases such as a request for help, or an update, give the reader no reason to prioritize the message.
A useful subject line therefore states the purpose of the email in a few specific words.
By contrast, mentioning the topic and any deadline allows the recipient to judge the urgency at a glance.
The same clarity helps later, when a person needs to find the message among hundreds of others.
quests.hint: "By contrast" and "the same clarity" compare and link the sentences. Which earlier sentences do they refer to?
quests.explanation: The problem of attention comes first, "therefore" leads to advice, vague phrases are a bad example, "by contrast" gives the good example, "the same clarity" adds a later benefit, and "thus" summarizes the advantage for both sides.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Automated programs called crawlers continuously follow links from page to page and record what they find.
When a query arrives, the engine identifies the pages in the index that contain relevant terms and then ranks them by several hundred criteria.
The recorded content is organized into an enormous index, much like the index at the back of a book.
These criteria include how recently a page was updated, how many other reputable sites refer to it, and how well it matches the intent of the search.
Because the criteria change regularly, the order of results for a given query can shift from month to month.
When a person types a query into a search engine, the results appear in a fraction of a second, but the work behind them began long before.
quests.hint: The opening idea promises unseen work behind the results. Which sentence introduces the earliest stage of that work?
quests.explanation: The instant results are described, the crawlers gather content, the content becomes an index, the query triggers matching and ranking, "these criteria" explains the ranking, and the last sentence explains why results change. "Before" in the first sentence means before the query.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: When Pallavi was reassigned to another department, she had two weeks to hand over her projects to a colleague.
By the time she left, the clients had barely noticed the change, which she regarded as the best measure of a successful handover.
During her final week, she remained available for questions but let her colleague take the lead in meetings.
She began by writing a summary of each project, listing its goals, its current status, and any problems that remained unresolved.
Next, she introduced her colleague to the key clients so that they would know whom to contact in the future.

quests.hint: One clause fixes a step in the timeline by referring to something already done. Which step must come before it?
quests.explanation: The reassignment sets a deadline, the summaries come first, the introductions follow, the folders come after the introductions, the final week reduces her role, and the last sentence evaluates the result. "The change" refers to the switch of contact person.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Engineers calculate their size according to the local range of temperatures, which can exceed fifty degrees between winter and summer.

Anyone who has driven over a large bridge has probably felt a rhythmic bump at certain points along the road.
Without gaps to absorb the movement, the materials would push against each other with enormous force and might crack or buckle.
These bumps are caused by expansion joints, which are gaps deliberately built into the structure.
quests.hint: "The joints" and "their size" both need something to have been introduced. Which sentence introduces the joints?
quests.explanation: The everyday experience comes first, the bumps are explained by expansion joints, the science of expansion explains why they are needed, "without gaps" describes the alternative, "therefore" describes the solution, and the last sentence refers to the size of the joints. "The movement" refers to expansion and contraction.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: The annual customer survey, completed by more than four thousand people, produced a mixed picture of the company's performance.
The next survey will show whether these measures have restored confidence in the service.
Satisfaction with product quality reached its highest level in five years, and respondents particularly praised the durability of the newer models.
The company has therefore introduced an online chat service and hired additional staff to reduce the pressure on the helpline.
Analysis of the comments showed that the complaints came mainly from a period when two support centers had been merged.
In contrast, ratings for after-sales support declined, with many customers complaining about long waiting times on the telephone helpline.
quests.hint: "Mixed picture" promises both good and bad news. Which sentence gives the good, and which gives the bad?
quests.explanation: The overview announces mixed results, the positive result comes next, "in contrast" introduces the negative result, the analysis explains its cause, "therefore" leads to the company's action, and the last sentence looks ahead. "These measures" refers to the chat service and extra staff.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: Because high pressure rarely causes noticeable symptoms, regular measurement is the only reliable way of detecting it.
A reading that is consistently above the recommended range forces the heart and vessels to work harder than they should.
Over years, this strain can damage the arteries and increase the risk of heart disease and stroke.
It is recorded as two numbers, the higher of which is measured when the heart contracts and the lower when it relaxes between beats.
Blood pressure is the force with which the heart pushes blood against the walls of the arteries.
Physicians therefore advise adults to have their pressure checked periodically, even when they feel perfectly well.
quests.hint: "It" and "this strain" both refer to earlier ideas. Which sentences introduce them?
quests.explanation: The definition comes first, "it" refers to blood pressure and explains the numbers, a high reading creates strain, "this strain" leads to long-term damage, "because" explains why measurement matters, and "therefore" leads to advice. "Even when they feel perfectly well" links back to the lack of symptoms.

quests.instruction: Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a logical paragraph.
shuffledSentences: The first task is to inform the local council, which may require a formal application if the road needs to be closed.
After the event, thanking everyone who helped and sharing photographs encourages people to take part again next year.
Once permission has been granted, neighbors can be invited by a leaflet that gives the date, the time, and a contact number.
A backup plan in case of rain on that day avoids disappointment and can be as simple as reserving a nearby hall.
Organizing a street party involves more paperwork than most residents expect, and the process should begin at least two months in advance.
